comparison: Both strongly support the core finding of early divergence and later convergence in gap gene expression patterns (C2, C3, C18, C24-C30, C69-C70, C82). OpenEval emphasizes the quantitative rigor of the dataset, while peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge this as the manuscript's central observational finding.

Perfect agreement on claims C19, C32, C33, C72. Both evaluations support the mechanistic explanation linking altered bcd distribution to posterior gap gene positioning, with neither raising concerns about this causal relationship.

Disagreement on certainty level for caudal-related claims (C20, C34-C36, C73). OpenEval finds the evidence supportive based on functional experiments, while peer reviewers express uncertainty and request clarification about whether effects are due to maternal versus zygotic cad.

Strong agreement on network structure conservation (C4, C44, C49). OpenEval emphasizes reciprocal repressive interactions, while peer reviewers explicitly endorse that network connectivity and regulatory signs remain intact despite quantitative differences in interaction strengths (C5, C45-C47, C53, C57-C58, C75).

Both support altered interaction strengths between species (C5, C45-C47, C53, C58, C75-C76). OpenEval provides detailed analysis of quantitative differences, while peer reviewers acknowledge these as parametric differences within conserved network structure.

Agreement on specific RNAi functional results (C42-C43, C48, C50-C52, C54-C55). OpenEval details the quantitative evidence from boundary shifts, while peer reviewers accept the comprehensive functional approach without challenging specific results.

Both support asymmetry in gap gene interactions (C56-C57). OpenEval notes the systematic evidence for posterior-to-anterior repression dominance, while peer reviewers implicitly accept this as part of the overall network structure findings.

Agreement on terminal gap gene RNAi results (C60-C66). OpenEval emphasizes synergistic effects in double knockdowns, while peer reviewers accept the functional data as part of the comprehensive quantitative analysis.

Both support conservation of terminal gap gene function (C67-C68). OpenEval notes comparison with published D. melanogaster phenotypes, while peer reviewers implicitly accept these findings through overall endorsement of functional analysis.

Strong agreement on the hourglass model interpretation (C1, C6, C77-C79, C82). OpenEval synthesizes experimental findings into this mechanistic framework, while peer reviewers explicitly endorse that genetic drift yields parametric differences with conserved network structure.

Both address the broader speculation about developmental system drift (C7). OpenEval explicitly labels this as uncertain and extending beyond the data, while peer reviewers do not challenge the extrapolation and implicitly accept it through publication endorsement.

Both support the causal relationship between maternal gradient differences and gap gene expression (C71, related to C19, C32-C33, C72). OpenEval emphasizes demonstrated causal relationships, while peer reviewers accept the connection between altered maternal inputs and gap gene differences.

Agreement on experimental methodology (C22-C23, C83-C87). OpenEval details the well-documented protocols and appropriate controls, while peer reviewers acknowledge the comprehensive quantitative analysis without questioning methods.

Perfect agreement on cuticle phenotype validation (C37, C103-C107). Both evaluations support that RNAi phenotypes appropriately recapitulate loss-of-function conditions and validate functional conservation between species.

Agreement on conservation of overall gap gene pattern with quantitative differences (C40, C39). OpenEval notes subtle differences in domain overlaps, while peer reviewers acknowledge conservation with quantitative variation consistent with altered interaction strengths.
Perfect agreement on the quantitative expression atlas data (C88-C102). Both evaluations accept the comprehensive dataset with precise spatial and temporal measurements without challenge.

OpenEval evaluates background/context claims (C8-C17) as supported by literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers focused on novel findings rather than established background knowledge.

Related to maternal factor effects (C71 vs C20, C34-C36, C73). OpenEval supports causal relationships between maternal factors and gap gene patterns, while peer reviewers express uncertainty specifically about maternal versus zygotic cad contributions.
